newsitem.title: USA: Clinton appeals Whitewater court ruling.
newsitem.headline: Clinton appeals Whitewater court ruling.

text.p: The White House Friday said it was appealing a court ruling that ordered the release of notes taken by a White House lawyer during a conversation with first lady Hillary Rodham Clinton.

"The court's holding undercuts this president's, and all future presidents', ability to seek candid and confidential legal advice," White House legal counsel Charles Ruff said in announcing the decision.

The U.S. Court of Appeals for the Eighth Circuit ruled that attorney-client privilege did not apply when Mrs. Clinton had a private conversation with Jane Sherburne, who was then with the White House legal counsel's office.
Kenneth Starr, the independent counsel looking into the Whitewater affair, had asked that Sherburne's notes be made available for a grand jury.
Ruff, in a statement, said that "until this ruling, the attorney-client privilege was universally assumed to apply to the work of private and government lawyers alike."
